details:
ADAPT-X is an AI-assisted astronaut health intelligence platform designed to explore the physiological challenges associated with long-duration spaceflight. It brings together an interactive 3D anatomical digital twin, physiological telemetry visualization, predictive analytics, and counterfactual simulation in a unified mission-control interface.

The platform explores five key dimensions of astronaut health: cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, metabolic, neurological, and behavioural. Through its interactive dashboard, users can examine physiological indicators, explore adaptation-related trends, and investigate hypothetical scenarios to better understand how the human body may respond to the space environment.

ADAPT-X incorporates NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) study metadata and uses synthetic telemetry for its interactive demonstration. This allows users to explore simulated physiological changes and adaptation scenarios. Its analytical features are intended for exploratory research and educational purposes, not clinical diagnosis or medically validated predictions.

The project uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, and React Three Fiber to deliver its interactive web experience. The application is deployed through Render, and its source code is publicly available on GitHub.

The creative approach behind ADAPT-X is the integration of anatomical visualization, physiological data exploration, and AI-assisted analytical concepts into a single interactive environment. By making complex space-health information easier to understand and explore, ADAPT-X aims to support future research, astronaut health-monitoring strategies, and long-duration mission planning.
